newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-KEARNS'S INJURY WOES DEEPEN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-KEARNS'S INJURY WOES DEEPEN.

text.p: Former Australia captain Phil Kearns, whose career has been beset by injuries for the past 20 months, faces a further three weeks on the sidelines after undergoing knee surgery on Tuesday.
The New South Wales hooker opted for an operation after suffering persistent swelling in his right knee after matches this season.
"Phil needed the surgery to clear up some irritation under the knee cap," New South Wales team physiopherapist Ian Collier said.
Kearns missed the whole of last season because of an Achilles tendon injury. He was first sidelined by an unrelated knee injury in August 1995.
The burly front row forwarcd, capped 49 times by Australia, has lost his place in New South Wales's starting line-up this season after struggling for match fitness because of his lengthy lay-off.
